name: 1x8 5F1 TWEED
description: A single eight-inch speaker in a small tweed box. Almost no low end, all midrange — which is why tiny amps record so well.

name: 1x8 PRINCETONE
description: The smallest Fender cabinet. Boxy and mid-forward, and it sounds far bigger through a microphone than in the room.

name: 1x10 BF PRINCETONE
description: A blackface ten-inch. Tight and clear with a little more bottom than an eight, and still very easy to record.

name: 1x10 METRO BLUES
description: A small Mesa ten-inch — rounder and less aggressive than the Fender equivalents.

name: 1x10 SF PRINCETONE
description: The silverface ten-inch. A touch brighter and stiffer than the blackface cabinet.

name: 1x12 AC20
description: A boutique twelve voiced for chime — open and airy, with the top end left alone.

name: 1x12 BLACK MAGICK
description: A Supro twelve. Dark, loose and characterful, nothing like a Fender or a Marshall.

name: 1x12 CAR AMBLER
description: An American-voiced boutique twelve with a clear top end and plenty of low end for its size.

name: 1x12 DELUXE TWEED
description: The tweed Deluxe cabinet. Warm and soft-edged, and it compresses when pushed.

name: 1x12 DELUXE VERB
description: The Deluxe Reverb cabinet — the reference twelve-inch clean sound, and on a huge number of records.

name: 1x12 DIV13 CJ11
description: A small boutique twelve, voiced for touch response rather than volume.

name: 1x12 G12T-100
description: A single Celestion G12T-100 — a high-power speaker with a scooped, modern voice made for heavy music.

name: 1x12 HOT KITTY
description: A boutique British-voiced twelve, brighter and more cutting than a Greenback.

name: 1x12 JR BLUES
description: The Blues Junior cabinet. Small, slightly boxy, and it starts to flap when you push it — which many people like.

name: 1x12 NUCLEAR TONE
description: A small dark twelve, made for the atmospheric reverb sounds the amp is known for.

name: 1x12 SCHOLZ
description: The twelve behind Tom Scholz's Boston sound — smooth and thick, with the harshness gone.

name: 1x12 TWEED 20112
description: A tweed-era twelve with a soft top end and a gentle midrange push.

name: 1x12 VIBRATO LUX
description: A brown-panel twelve — warmer and looser than a blackface cabinet.

name: 1x15 HEART KEY
description: A fifteen-inch speaker: rounder and slower than a twelve, with a low end that moves more air.

name: 1x15 PORTABASS
description: A compact bass fifteen, voiced for clarity rather than weight.

name: 1x15 VIBROVERB
description: The Vibroverb's fifteen. Looser and fatter than any Fender twelve, and a blues favourite for exactly that.

name: 2x10 HEART KEY
description: Two tens — tighter and faster than a twelve, with a midrange that cuts.

name: 2x10 SUPER 6G4
description: The brown Super's pair of tens. Punchy, mid-forward, and it stays defined when pushed.

name: 2x12 5153 STEALTH
description: A modern two-by-twelve voiced for the EVH amps — tight, scooped and aimed at heavy playing.

name: 2x12 65 BASSGUY
description: A blackface two-by-twelve. Clean, firm and uncoloured, which makes it a good platform for pedals.

name: 2x12 CHIEFMAN
description: A boutique British two-by-twelve with chime and considerable headroom.

name: 2x12 CLASS-A 30W
description: The AC30 cabinet, with its Celestion Blues. Chimey, compressed, and the reason a Vox sounds like a Vox.

name: 2x12 DOUBLE VERB
description: The Twin Reverb cabinet — big, clean and bright, the standard against which clean is measured.

name: 2x12 LEAD 80
description: A pair of Celestion Lead 80s — a harder, more modern voice than a vintage Celestion.

name: 2x12 TEXAS STAR
description: Mesa's two-by-twelve. Tight and even, with more low-end control than most open-backed cabinets.

name: 4x10 BASSGUY RI
description: The Bassman's four tens. The cabinet that made both blues guitar and early rock — punchy, mid-rich and loud.

name: 4x12 1960TV
description: The tall Marshall cabinet. Greenbacks, a deeper box, and a rounder low end than the later slant cabs.

name: 4x12 5153
description: The EVH four-by-twelve — modern, tight and built for high gain.

name: 4x12 5153 STEALTH
description: The Stealth version of the EVH cabinet, voiced a little darker.

name: 4x12 CITRUS
description: Orange's four-by-twelve. Thick, woody and mid-heavy, with none of the Marshall bite.

name: 4x12 FRIEDMAN GB
description: Friedman's cabinet with Greenbacks — vintage British voicing with modern build.

name: 4x12 FRIEDMAN V30
description: The same cabinet with Vintage 30s: brighter, harder and with a pronounced upper midrange.

name: 4x12 LERXST
description: The cabinet behind Alex Lifeson's sound — British-voiced with a clear, articulate top end.

name: 4x12 RECTO SLANT
description: Mesa's slant Rectifier cab with Vintage 30s. The nineties and after: tight, aggressive and directional.

name: 4x12 RECTO STRAIGHT
description: The straight Rectifier cabinet — the same speakers with a little more low end than the slant.

name: 4x12 RUMBLE EV12L
description: A four-by-twelve with EV12Ls. Enormous headroom and a very flat response — the hi-fi end of guitar cabinets.

name: 4x12 RUMBLE EV12S
description: The other EV loading, with a slightly softer top end.

name: 4x12 SOLO 100
description: The Soldano cabinet — smooth, even, and voiced to flatter high gain rather than sharpen it.

name: 4x12 USA MC90
description: Mesa's cabinet with MC90s. Warmer and less scooped than a Vintage 30 cab.

name: 8x10 SV BASS
description: The Ampeg fridge. Eight tens moving as one — the loud bass cabinet, and the one on most rock records.
